name: connect-model-main-build
description: What: Build the Connect model on the Main instance from the spec (empty-model bootstrap): delete this family if present (the 5 PData entities, the retired names PDataProfiseeExport, PDataProfiseeToProfiseeImport, then the 50 Dba domains), create the domains with their spec ids, load their rows, create the 5 PData entities (120 attributes each), verify. Never deletes another entity; stops first if another entity uses a Dba domain. Why: A building block of the Connect pack; a test, setup or schedule workload runs it so its steps exist once. When: Never run directly once the pack is tested; its parents run it. Running it alone is safe only when its own Needs are met. Needs: reference values: connect/instances:ProfiseeInstanceName, connect/machines:ApplicationServerNameFQDN. Success: Every step Succeeded or Skipped. If it fails: Run connect-preflight first; then open the first failed step, whose If it fails text names what to check.
globalParametersNotes: Spec: C:\devops\repos\speed-merchants\CrewChief\connect-model-spec. Entity globals are name -> name so a rename is one edit. Ids are deterministic per entity name; domain ids come from the spec.

inline.description: What: Gateway check: list entities. Accepts ONLY 200 so a wrong address (404) or a wrong key (401) stops the run before anything is created or deleted. Why: Calls the Profisee or TestAuto REST API for this change or check, the same way a client would. Success: The response status is one of the expected codes (200). If it fails: 401 = the API key is not set on that instance yet (run connect-setup) or the secret is wrong; 404 = the record, entity or address is missing; no response = the server in the URL (connect/urls, connect/machines) is down.

What: Fail fast when the instance's Maestro model id differs from the spec (spec.json modelId), before anything is deleted or created. Why: Does work no single built-in step does (several calls, waits or checks in one place) and stops at the first problem. Success: The script finishes without an error; its output lines say what it did. If it fails: Read the last output line and the error text: the script names the value, server or record it could not handle.

What: Delete this family if present (absent is fine): 7 entities, then the 50 Dba domains. Warns about other entities and leaves them alone; stops before deleting anything if one of them uses a Dba domain. Why: Does work no single built-in step does (several calls, waits or checks in one place) and stops at the first problem. Success: The script finishes without an error; its output lines say what it did. If it fails: Read the last output line and the error text: the script names the value, server or record it could not handle.
